explanation: Traverse left before right and append only nodes with neither child. This produces the leaf values in their left-to-right order.
timeComplexity: O(n) time. Append-based versions visit each node once; Python’s returned-list concatenation adds repeated copying of descendant leaf lists.
spaceComplexity: O(h) recursion space plus O(l) output for l leaves. Append variants use height-sized recursion plus one output per leaf; Python also creates temporary concatenated lists.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: The recursive traversal visits every node once and appends a value exactly when that node has no children. All leaves of a left subtree appear before every leaf of its right subtree, and the recursion respects that order at every node. Thus the result contains every leaf exactly once, in left-to-right order, without including internal nodes.
walkthrough: For [16, 7, 25, 2, 11, null, 30, null, 4], the leftmost leaf is 4 beneath node 2. Next comes leaf 11, then leaf 30 in the right subtree. Internal nodes 16, 7, 2 and 25 are not appended. Return [4, 11, 30]. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: A null tree has no leaves.
A one-node tree contributes its root as a leaf.
Different leaves with equal Data values are both retained.
